stories.summary: Three years after Maui wildfires many still struggle with ‘biological, emotional and social consequences’, study says A spate of ferocious wildfires across North America and Europe, worsened by the climate crisis, has incinerated homes and forests and forced thousands of people to flee. stories.summary: Data shows Canadians have replaced US vacations with other international trips in apparent rebuke to Trump Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to the US in 2025 than in the previous year, as Donald Trump’s hostile policies towards his northern neighbour continue to incur an economic cost, new government data shows. stories.summary: New research linking the issue to Parkinson’s disease adds to the evidence of serious health repercussions from traffic volume and other sources The roar of late-night traffic is not just annoying for those trying to sleep. It can also have profound effects on their health. A pioneering new study, published this month, has found a clear link between road noise and Parkinson’s disease. stories.title: US bans humanoid robots from China, citing ‘unacceptable risks’
stories.summary: Move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US The Federal Communications Commission announced a ban on humanoid robots from China on Tuesday, saying that the technology poses “unacceptable risks” to the country’s national security. The move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US. stories.title: Kenya investigating unexpected deaths of 15 elephants in national park
stories.summary: Potential toxic substance detected in several of 15 elephants found dead in Kenya’s Amboseli national park Officials are investigating the deaths of 15 elephants over the past month in Kenya’s Amboseli national park. The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) said 10 of the elephants showed signs of partial paralysis before dying within two days. Continue reading...

stories.title: As US-Iran war rages, who's risking the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Though Iran continues to attack vessels as leverage in its war with the United States, data show that several shippers continue to transit the waterway.

stories.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern and WAFCON
stories.summary: Bernadette Amani joined Bayern Munich in January and is now captaining Ivory Coast in their first WAFCON in 12 years. Getting to the top hasn't been a straight path for the newly crowned German double winner.

stories.title: Why is Germany building roads for yesterday's climate?
stories.summary: As the Autobahn buckles under heat waves, Germany is still paving roads for a past climate. Engineers know how to fix that — so what's the holdup?

stories.title: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.

stories.title: Fact check: Berlin Pride attack claims debunked
stories.summary: Following the Islamist terrorist attack at Berlin Pride, rumors, false claims and misleading videos have been spreading on social media. DW Fact check examines some of the most widely shared claims.

stories.title: FIFA plans to form new commercial subsidiary and sell stake
stories.summary: FIFA has announced plans to form a commercial subsidiary and to sell a non-controlling interest to private investors. It needs approval from member associations, but is claiming that it will benefit them financially.

stories.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party protest victory signals trouble ahead for Modi
stories.summary: Ally forced to resign, with opposition parties reinvigorated and strongman leader’s grip over media channels rocked Even the night before Narendra Modi accepted the resignation of his education minister, India’s prime minister appeared confident that the largest mass uprising to take place in his 12 years in power would do little to rattle his government. stories.title: FIFA boss Infantino takes aim at World Cup critics
stories.summary: In a strongly worded open statement, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has hit out at those he says were too "consumed by hate and criticism" to enjoy the tournament. Infantino brushed off a number of corruption concerns.

stories.title: Firefighters in Spain and France battle raging wildfires – video
stories.summary: Footage shows the extent of the devastation caused by wildfires in Cenicientos, in the Madrid region of Spain, on Friday. Members of Spain's military emergency unit sought to contain the blazes in the Madrid region and in Cuevas de Cañart in the country's north-east. stories.summary: A wildfire burning in Spain's eastern Castellón province has grown beyond firefighting capacity, the Valencia regional government has said. Wildfires in Spain and France have driven more than 300,000 people to flee their homes and holiday accommodation. stories.title: Shots fired near US consulate in Canada for second time in four months
stories.summary: No one was injured and no suspects have been identified in connection to shooting near Toronto compound, police say Shots were fired near the US consulate in Toronto early on Monday but no one was injured in the second shooting near the diplomatic compound in four months. “Officers heard a firearm being discharged in the area,” and “a white sedan was seen fleeing the scene”, Toronto police said on X. Continue reading...

stories.title: Pinochet-era soldier jailed for killing folk singer Víctor Jara 53 years ago
stories.summary: Nelson Haase Mazzei was sentenced for murdering Jara in 2023, but fled from authorities in Chile More than 50 years after the murder of the Chilean folk singer Víctor Jara , the last man wanted in connection with his death has been tracked down and brought to justice. Nelson Haase Mazzei, a retired colonel, fled from authorities in 2023 after he and six other retired soldiers were sentenced in absentia for murdering Jara and another man. Continue reading...

stories.title: Who has the momentum in the Russia-Ukraine war? – video explainer
stories.summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, the war in Ukraine has changed dramatically. The Guardian's Luke Harding looks at who has the advantage in the war now and how Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy's strategy has shifted Continue reading...

stories.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
stories.summary: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

stories.title: Serbia's LGBTQ+ community faces 'epidemic of violence'
stories.summary: Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have never been higher. The attacks are part of a larger shift in society targeting marginalized people.

stories.title: WAFCON 2026: What you need to know
stories.summary: Several months after it was supposed to start and with more teams than first planned, WAFCON 2026 is finally set to begin. The hosts want a maiden title while a tournament outsider have one of its best players.

stories.title: Berlin Pride: Latest in string of deadly vehicle attacks
stories.summary: The attack at a Berlin Pride event is only the most recent incident on a long list where vehicles were used as weapons. The US, Canada, and China also saw similar attacks in recent years.

stories.title: Berlin Pride attack: What we know so far
stories.summary: On Saturday, a vehicle drove into a crowd near a Christopher Street Day celebration in what is being regarded as an attack on the LGBTQ+ community. The main suspect has since been confronted and shot dead.

stories.title: Berlin Pride ramming: Police shoot suspect dead
stories.summary: Police said the suspect was shot dead in an operation, after the incident was classified as an "Islamist terrorist" attack. One person was killed and several others injured in the attack.

stories.title: Car ramming attacks: Why do they keep happening?
stories.summary: Cars are being used as weapons, to ram, kill and maim innocent people. The reasons why are not always clear, nor are solutions to preventing such attacks.

stories.title: 'Amnesia' about measles risk and low vaccination rates have helped US infections grow
stories.summary: The latest US data show measles cases from January to mid-July 2026 totaled more than all cases in 2025. Experts blame a fall in vaccination and warn that people have forgotten measles can be life-threatening.

stories.title: Germany: Islamist terror attack on Berlin Pride parade triggers political debate
stories.summary: Following the terrorist attack on Berlin's Pride parade, the Christopher Street Day parade, politicians and security experts are demanding consequences.

stories.title: German Chancellor Merz completes cabinet reshuffle
stories.summary: After days of confusion, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has reshuffled his cabinet. Conservative politicians fear that this will not help with the prospects in the upcoming state elections.

stories.title: EU rejects suspending biometric border controls despite 20 ‘difficult spots’
stories.summary: Officials admit new post-Brexit EES system is ‘not perfect’, as airports and airlines voice fears over delays The EU has rejected calls by airports and airlines to suspend the implementation of new fingerprinting and facial recognition border controls even though it admits there are “20 difficult spots” with queue chaos. stories.summary: Disruption at Channel crossings expected to rise amid new fingerprint and facial recognition checks France and the UK have agreed to increase staffing at border controls in response to warnings of travel chaos caused by new fingerprinting and facial recognition checks.
